build_policy: retain the Lake Superior portion of the joined upper-Great-Lakes GSHHG L2 feature
select the shortest accepted St. Marys water cross-section in the frozen search window
require shoreline-snapped endpoints, zero GSHHG L3 land crossing, and separation of Superior and Huron references
close the accepted 2.21 km St. Marys gate as land, never as an OBC
preserve the independently inventoried 45 GSHHG L3 islands as hole loops
preserve every retained source shoreline vertex and both artificial closure anchors

source_policy: NOAA NCEI ETOPO 2022 15 arc-second full-lake surface elevation
bathymetry.coverage_requirement: finite positive depth at every accepted wet-domain cell center, with a GSHHG-derived wet mask and complete interpolation support around the boundary

preparation: Select the cached GSHHG 2.3.7 high-resolution L2 upper-Great-Lakes feature.
Retain Lake Superior with one deterministic water-only St. Marys numerical land gate.
Preserve all contained GSHHG L3 islands.
Fetch a request-bounded ETOPO 2022 15 arc-second full-lake subset.
Convert ETOPO elevation to positive-down depth using 183.2 m IGLD 1985 LWD.
notes: This manifest belongs to the three-case boundary-continuity experiment, not the archived six-case matrix.
This is a zero-OBC closed-lake contract case and must write no NS records.
The selected St. Marys gate is a 2.21 km numerical land boundary near 46.478 degrees north with two shoreline-snapped hard anchors and zero L3-land crossing.
ETOPO elevation uses EGM2008 and the 183.2 m lake LWD uses IGLD 1985; no vertical datum transformation is claimed.
Preparation readiness is bound to the exact versioned validation artifact and its active boundary/bathymetry hashes before meshing.
